title: Watchlist
description: Which names look strongest, which are sitting at the bottom of their range, and which are too thinly traded to size into.

panels.title: Market breadth today
panels.description: Share of the tracked universe that closed up. Context for everything below: a strong name in a weak market is a different proposition.

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT ROUND(advancing_pct,1) AS "Advancing" FROM v_market_breadth ORDER BY session_date DESC LIMIT 1

panels.title: Stocks reading bullish
panels.description: Close and the 5-day average both above the 20-day average.

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT COUNT(*) AS "Bullish" FROM v_bullish_ranking WHERE trend_score = 2

panels.title: Stocks in the bottom decile of their 52-week range
panels.description: How many sit in the lowest tenth of their range over the past year.

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT COUNT(*) AS "Bottom decile" FROM v_range_context WHERE pct_of_52w_range <= 10
targets.queryText: SELECT COUNT(*) AS "Bottom decile" FROM v_range_context WHERE pct_of_52w_range <= 10

panels.title: The 5 strongest setups right now
panels.description: Ranked by: distance above the 20-day average (%) + the 5-day return (%) + (RSI-50)/10, less a penalty above RSI 75. This describes momentum that already exists - a ranking of current strength, not a forecast. Nothing here knows anything about tomorrow.

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT b.symbol                       AS "Symbol",
       ROUND(b.bullish_score, 2)            AS "Score",
       b.session_date                       AS "As of",
       b.open                               AS "Open",
       b.high                               AS "High",
       b.low                                AS "Low",
       b.close                              AS "Close",
       ROUND(b.pct_above_sma20, 2)          AS "vs SMA20 %",
       ROUND(b.ret5, 2)                     AS "5-day %",
       ROUND(b.rsi14, 1)                    AS "RSI(14)",
       w.week52_high                        AS "52w high",
       w.week52_low                         AS "52w low",
       r.high_10                            AS "10d high",
       r.low_10                             AS "10d low",
       ROUND(r.pct_of_10d_range, 1)         AS "% of 10d range"
FROM v_bullish_ranking b
JOIN instrument i ON i.symbol = b.symbol
LEFT JOIN symbol_week52 w ON w.instrument_id = i.id
LEFT JOIN (SELECT symbol, high_10, low_10, pct_of_10d_range,
                  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY symbol ORDER BY session_date DESC) AS rn
           FROM v_range_position) r ON r.symbol = b.symbol AND r.rn = 1
ORDER BY b.bullish_score DESC
LIMIT 5

panels.title: Bottom 10% of the 52-week range (or as far back as data goes)
panels.description: Where price sits between the 52-week low and high. The 10-day figure is kept alongside, because they answer different questions: ten sessions says where a stock sits this fortnight, a year says whether it is genuinely near a low. 'Sessions behind it' is how many daily candles back the range - anything well short of ~248 is not really a year. Near a low is not the same as cheap; a name can sit there while it keeps falling.

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT symbol                        AS "Symbol",
       close                              AS "Close",
       week52_low                         AS "52w low",
       week52_high                        AS "52w high",
       ROUND(pct_of_52w_range, 1)         AS "% of 52w range",
       ROUND(pct_of_10d_range, 1)         AS "% of 10d range",
       low_10                             AS "10d low",
       high_10                            AS "10d high",
       week52_sessions                    AS "Sessions behind it"
FROM v_range_context
WHERE pct_of_52w_range <= 10
ORDER BY pct_of_52w_range

panels.title: Bottom decile by value actually traded (10-day average)
panels.description: The other reading of "bottom 10 percentile of market value": the least liquid names, by rupees changing hands per day rather than by price position. Worth knowing before sizing a position in one of them. This one stays on a 10-day window on purpose: liquidity is about what is trading now, not what traded last winter.

targets.rawQueryText:
WITH latest AS (
  SELECT symbol, close, avg_daily_turnover_10,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY symbol ORDER BY session_date DESC) AS rn
  FROM v_range_position),
current AS (SELECT * FROM latest WHERE rn = 1),
cutoff AS (SELECT avg_daily_turnover_10 AS threshold FROM current
           ORDER BY avg_daily_turnover_10
           LIMIT 1 OFFSET (SELECT CAST(COUNT(*) * 0.1 AS INTEGER) FROM current))
SELECT c.symbol                        AS "Symbol",
       c.close                         AS "Close",
       ROUND(c.avg_daily_turnover_10)  AS "Avg daily value traded (10d)"
FROM current c, cutoff
WHERE c.avg_daily_turnover_10 <= cutoff.threshold
ORDER BY c.avg_daily_turnover_10
